data.body_html:
September 2027 is the sweet spot for a Marbella boat rental. The summer crowds have thinned, the sea is still a balmy 26°C, and you get 8 hours of daily sunshine with light winds. This shoulder-season weather guide covers everything you need to know — temperatures, sea conditions, best boats, and insider tips — so you can plan the perfect day on the water from Puerto Banús.

September 2027 Weather Overview for Marbella

September in Marbella delivers near-perfect boating weather. Average daytime highs hit 28°C, with sea temperatures peaking at 26–27°C early in the month. Winds are predominantly light easterlies at 5–10 knots, creating calm sea states ideal for families and first-timers. Humidity drops to around 60%, making it comfortable even in the midday sun. Sunset occurs around 20:30, giving you long evenings for golden-hour cruises along the Golden Mile.

Sea Conditions and Visibility

The Mediterranean off Marbella in September is remarkably clear, with underwater visibility often exceeding 15 metres. This makes it a prime month for snorkelling at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Swell heights average 0.3–0.8 metres, with occasional 1-metre waves during easterly breezes. For the smoothest ride, book a morning charter (10:00–14:00) when the sea is flattest. Our licensed skippers know the best sheltered coves, such as Cabopino and the Río Verde estuary.

Best Boats for September Weather

With stable conditions, almost any boat in our fleet works well. For groups wanting speed and luxury, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for 4 hours (includes a free jet ski) is a top pick. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers shaded upper-deck lounging — perfect for the midday heat. Budget-conscious groups can opt for the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both €749/2h → €2,299/8h), ideal for 9–11 guests. For a romantic sunset, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) is a nimble choice.

What’s Included in Your September Charter

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). You also get unlimited water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. In September, we recommend bringing extra sunscreen and a hat — the sun is still strong. All boats depart from Puerto Banús, so you can start your day with a coffee at one of the marina cafés before heading out.

Itinerary Suggestions for September

  • Half-day (4h): Cruise south to Cala del Faro for swimming and snorkelling, then along the coast to Cabopino for lunch. Return via the Marbella Marina skyline.
  • Full-day (8h): Head east to Cala Cortés and Sotogrande for a longer beach stop, then west to Estepona for a seafood lunch. Perfect for groups wanting a full Mediterranean experience.
  • Sunset charter (2–3h): Depart at 17:00, anchor off the Golden Mile, and watch the sun dip behind La Concha mountain. Includes cava and canapés.

Booking Tips for September 2027

September is shoulder season, so availability is better than peak summer, but popular boats like the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) and Mangusta 80 still book 2–3 weeks ahead. For last-minute plans, smaller vessels like the Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) or Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) are often available with 3–5 days’ notice. Check the 7-day forecast before booking, and consider a morning charter for the calmest seas. For pricing on boats not in Tier A or B, simply contact us via WhatsApp.
